# Pandemonium and Ibuki: wanted company, unequal care, and the right to answer

## 0. Responsibility and evidence boundary

This study owns a shared question: how Pandemonium's members make company with Ibuki when affection, office, dependence, pleasure and coercion pull in different directions. Its existing ensemble home contains two substantial named responsibilities, Makoto→Ibuki and Iroha→Ibuki. They are retained as distinct directions within this one parent, with Ibuki's answers central to each. They are not two additional denominator packages. The separate institutional question about Pandemonium's roles, resources and selective care, the Kayoko–Ako boundary question, and the five individual character monographs remain separate responsibilities. An accepted character portrait cannot stand in for this account of encounters, changed participation and competing recipients.

The current maintained Gehenna private argument is used at its complete substantive adoption body, lines420–602. The complete accepted GROUP1901–1902 and MINI32 arguments and the complete EVENT833,835 and860 arguments were received here. Twenty-two small MAIN/checkpoint analytical owners were also received completely at their recorded scopes. Seven additional exact-bound public context copies supply navigation only and are not claimed as newly received whole arguments. The input receipt distinguishes those predicates. This is synthesis of admitted written meanings, not a fresh reading of every underlying private episode, whole memorial scene, primary Japanese source, recorded performance or corpus route. Earlier producer frontiers, pending admissions and next-reading instructions within dated source owners retain their historical meaning; current Cycle008 and adopted controls determine present admission and readiness.

The account therefore allows strong local conclusions without constructing a hidden biography. The pudding trilogy can establish an actual refusal, a wider promise and forgiven offense. It cannot establish that all future puddings were replaced, that every office action became legitimate, or that it occurs immediately before the separate Final rescue. The two named duties retain the same full original fourteen gaps as OPEN. Receiving and exact binding do not constitute ROOT literary acceptance, named-duty completion, a model promotion or a milestone claim.

## 1. Core thesis: company survives through differentiated answers

Pandemonium's company with Ibuki is strongest where a member stops treating her affection as a guaranteed return. Makoto can love her company while wanting her admiration, treating her comfort selectively, or borrowing her innocence to make a leadership scene appealing. Iroha can recognize her preferences and offer protection while wanting quiet, leaving the organization, hiding information, or using her hurt to increase a punishment. Ibuki can enjoy both members, be frightened, make mistakes, want to help and refuse a proposed return. These directions do not add up to one benevolent family essence or one covertly manipulative machine. Their repeated encounters put the recipients' answers between a giver's account of care and the action that follows. ([Private account][PS01], Pandemonium paragraphs502–512; [pudding trilogy][PS35], §14; [MAIN return visit][PS14].)

A promise about pudding makes that distinction unusually clear. In MINI15030, Makoto's apology becomes acceptable when Ibuki asks her not to take **anyone's** pudding, not simply to remember that Ibuki's dessert is special. The finger promise and forgiveness are real represented ends. The ten replacement puddings remain Makoto's account, and no general account of future compliance follows. What changes in the encounter is the terms under which Ibuki agrees to resume company: her grievance is heard, her own answer is sought, and the wrong's scope widens beyond a favored child. That is a relational achievement with an unfinished afterlife, not an institutional acquittal. ([MINI32][PS35], §14, MINI15030:u0088–0114.)

Iroha's offered exit establishes a different achievement. In MAIN S2V002C2E011, she offers Ibuki hair combing, reading and company away from the changed Makoto. Ibuki likes the offer and nevertheless chooses to remain because Makoto is lonely. Iroha checks that this is what she wants and accepts the answer. Respect is visible in the option and in accepting refusal of that option. It would be an error to count only removal from Makoto as protective care, just as it would be an error to turn Ibuki's choice into proof that the environment is safe or that she understands every political danger. The scene gives an answer to an offered course of action; its worth is not cancelled by the missing safety certificate. ([MAIN return visit][PS14], u0041–0110.)

The ensemble's ordinary ends make those answers intelligible. Ibuki wants to play, taste things, make a collage, see a parade, help with work and spend time with people she likes. Iroha wants rest and chosen reading, not only the opportunity to serve. Makoto wants admired company and sometimes obtains it through genuine practical adjustment. Satsuki wants relief, food and reassuring contact; Chiaki wants scenes worth seeing and recording. These are ends whose partial achievement and frustration matter before they become examples of political virtue or crisis resilience. A child wanting more time with PS68 is not valuable only because the request chastens a leader. A quiet outing is not discarded because no government changes. ([Private account][PS01], paragraphs502–510; [MINI32][PS35], §§12,14; [summer account][PS04], 001–015.)

The synthesis is consequently about the distribution of choice within shared participation. Makoto and Iroha differ in what they notice, offer, withhold and ask back. Ibuki's agency is neither adult sovereignty nor passive moral symbolism. The social structure permits real kindness and real asymmetry together. It changes locally when members act on an answer that complicates their own preferred story: a refused return, a refusal to obey a stay order, a child who already knows about a quarrel, or a member who does not want another photograph. No uniform affection score can replace these encounters. ([MINI32][PS35], §14; [summer account][PS04], 004–005,012–014.)

## 2. Longitudinal arc: locally ordered changes, independent recurring contexts

Three internally ordered sequences provide the strongest changes. The MINI150 trilogy moves from a repeated pudding offense and Ibuki's departure, through discovery and chosen play with PS68, to the apology, wider promise and farewell. MAIN S2V002 moves from the abnormal drive toward unanimity, through Iroha's departure and the private return visit, to coordinated resistance, local recovery, Makoto's apology and public promises. EVENT860 moves through the narrated drifting days, disagreements, pirate-ship encounter, escape, medical aftermath and wanted continuing company. Each sequence gives development. Their coexistence is not a warrant to arrange every private variant and event into one maturation ladder. ([MINI32][PS35], §14; [MAIN checkpoints][PS06], [PS08]; [summer account][PS04], source-form and item accounts.)

Within the pudding sequence, departure is followed by encounter rather than immediate return. Ibuki is lost and feels sorry for harsh words while retaining a valid grievance about the theft. Aru offers an escort; Ibuki refuses it. When the searchers find her, she rejects a kidnapping interpretation and says she left voluntarily. Being no longer angry does not mean she is ready to stop playing. Her later forgiveness is situated after this interval of wanted company and her own condition on Makoto. Treating the middle as mere logistical delay would remove the child's independent time and make return a foregone adult objective. ([MINI32][PS35], MINI15010:u0064–0097; MINI15020:u0025–0077; MINI15030:u0088–0114.)

MAIN has a more severe local separation. Makoto's demand for unity depicts dissent as a defective screw; Iroha verbally leaves, and Makoto accepts that choice while later practical burdens show its cost. Chiaki notices the emptied social atmosphere and a hiatus in her newspaper. Ibuki is low and alone with a busy Makoto. Iroha's return visit expressly does not mean she has rejoined. Later she coordinates work across former opponents, appeals to Makoto under an unresolved counterbroadcast mechanism, and receives an actual apology. The movement is not private affection automatically transferring into a public cure. It involves distinct choices, other contributors and explicitly incomplete causal knowledge. ([MAIN departure][PS10]; [Chiaki interview][PS11]; [return visit][PS14]; [coalition][PS13], [PS18]; [recovery][PS19].)

The public aftermath preserves an important adverse remainder. Makoto withdraws the battle plan and promises property return, while students report ammunition not yet restored, unwanted contribution points and anxiety at another assembly. The freedom speech corrects a possessive formulation toward a shared Gehenna. Sensei's encouraging response does not dispose of the harmed students' claims. Nor does Iroha's call for familiar bluster prove that all members have recovered their former security. The local recovery and speech are achieved; restitution, recurrence prevention and technical explanation remain unfinished. Both kinds of end must survive the ensemble account. ([MAIN aftermath][PS20], u0001–0076,0140–0247.)

EVENT860 supplies a sequence of company that includes failures of recognition. Makoto's costly rental decision is real, and she immediately denies Ibuki's self-blame. Iroha spares the child worry, but Ibuki later reveals she already knows about their drifting and quarrel. Iroha's refusal to work is not fully met by an apology about volume. Makoto then refuses to order her to remain, articulating free choice even amid a badly managed situation. They later contribute differently to survival, quarrel and rescue, and return to wanted company. This arc cannot be rewritten as unbroken harmony or reduced to incompetent adults corrected by a pure child. ([Summer account][PS04], 002–005,007–014.)

The dream qualification also changes the arc's limits. EVENT860016–025 are retrospectively dream-qualified by026–027. Their forced assignments, kindness, battles and enjoyment can be read as the written account's staged possibilities and remembered concerns. They do not add literal conquest, verified biological identities or actual all-school enrollment to the earlier drifting narrative. Printed local flashback and day markers can organize the event internally; variants, release order, titles and retrieval order cannot locate it globally against MAIN or MINI. Likewise the two GROUP stories are independently staged contexts, not a proved before-and-after sequence. ([Summer account][PS04], 016–027 and synthesis; [GROUP account][PS05], source boundary.)

The Eden and Final appearances complicate, rather than complete, this development. In Eden, Iroha corrects Makoto's imagined Schale alliance, Makoto later self-claims a destructive Arius bargain, Ibuki sees dangerous boxes and an explosion follows. Rescue is later reported, and Iroha urges Makoto to rest in the epilogue. Final depicts an actual Toramaru arrival and locally cleared danger while Makoto and Ibuki give different pudding-and-help motives. Neither sequence authorizes attaching a single recurring pudding incident to all the others. The ensemble can repeat an interpretive pressure—favored company enabling and redirecting action—without asserting a shared global date or identical offense. ([Eden formal visit][PS24], [collusion][PS26], [rescue report][PS29], [epilogue][PS30]; [Final rescue][PS33].)

## 3. Public and private selves: care does not settle its recipients' claims

The private normal account restores kinds of attention that the public office plot cannot supply by itself. Makoto negotiates with merchants, adjusts care for Lionmaru, shops, accepts or views a photograph, experiences play and pudding, and makes do-not-touch boundaries in a written form. Some commercial remedies are unfinished; a broadly narrated resolution is not an inspected repayment. These differences permit a leader to have ordinary vulnerability and desirable company without retroactively certifying competence, generosity in every transaction or innocence in public misconduct. They also prevent interpreting every pleasant detail as merely a mask for domination. ([Private account][PS01], paragraph502 and whole-MM/mode qualifications546.)

Iroha's private sofa, coffee, reading and dinner matter as choices in their own right. Completed help, an arrival with coffee and cleaning before sunset are differentiated from invitations to future escape or imagined cohabitation. The adopted written-form correction preserves swimsuit/all-day-reading wording rather than inventing changed clothes or a hidden intervening activity. Those meanings should not be made to cause her MAIN resignation or coalition work. They do, however, make the costs of always being the practical caretaker legible: a preference for rest is not a failure of affection, and competence does not waive her right to choose whose demand to meet. ([Private account][PS01], paragraph504 and whole-body limits.)

Ibuki's private repertoire is equally resistant to summary as cuteness. Failed park, carousel and parade plans differ from actually fulfilled local games and pleasant time. She gets help down after finding shade; that is not independent descent. She actually eats corn and feels full in one context, while an offered rice ball elsewhere has no printed consumption. Her half-empty collage comes from too few collected materials rather than a fabricated lack of paper. Wanted careers conclude with partial understanding and thanks, not an enacted arrest, profession or meal. These small distinctions keep her initiative, frustration and appetite distinct from the adults' stories about what she needs. ([Private account][PS01], paragraph506.)

Satsuki's relief and appetite and Chiaki's curiosity broaden the ensemble beyond two rival carers. Satsuki's food, escort, hand-held reassurance and night paperwork coexist with failed methods, adults refusing, fatigue and exploiting vulnerability. Chiaki's shared newspaper, tasting, visits and excited return coexist with an unsuccessful tenth macaron, unusable images and lost notes. Encouragement does not recover her notebook or publish an article. In photographs and private contact, permission is particular: an invitation to look does not erase a later request not to look or to stay still, and departure or a withdrawn message does not become ongoing consent. Their own wants and limits are part of the company Ibuki joins. ([Private account][PS01], paragraphs508–510.)

Public care changes the recipient scale. In GROUP1902, cocoa is something Ibuki wants; Iroha uses its absence as an audit criterion against the Prefects. A hospitality wish thereby becomes institutional leverage. In Eden, Makoto's delight in a planned attack puts Ibuki in a dangerous airship despite her ordinary observation of its boxes. In MAIN, the prospect of turning everyone into gears destroys the very differences Chiaki values. The private goods are still real, but their local reality cannot answer the people exposed to public punishment or coerced unanimity. The ensemble's moral difficulty comes from retaining these separate recipients together. ([GROUP account][PS05], audit sequence; [Eden collusion][PS26]; [Chiaki interview][PS11].)

This is not a rule that private affection is irrelevant to public conduct. Final rescue shows Makoto's wish for Ibuki's favor contributing, by her own account, to helping other students, and Ibuki says she asked them to help. The descent of Toramaru and locally cleared danger are represented; the exact balance of motive and the earlier intelligence path are not independently inspected. Selective affection can have a wider good effect. It remains selective, and those helped need not certify the leader's other actions. The text allows gratitude without requiring a total character verdict. ([Final rescue][PS33], scene001:u0022–0061 and scene002:u0001–0024.)

## 4. School and club role: participation exceeds office, while labor still has costs

The ensemble lives within an office that distributes work unequally. Iroha's departure makes Makoto perform practical tasks herself; Chiaki sees a potential scoop in this change. The old newspaper's hiatus and the members' absence make the room less lively. These are social and administrative effects of a person's absence, not evidence that the organization has legally dissolved. The member is wanted partly for what she does and partly for the company she makes. A reading that names only labor extraction misses the latter; a reading that names only family affection conceals the former. ([MAIN Chiaki account][PS11], u0001–0014.)

Iroha's ordinary rest is therefore an interpretive check on office entitlement. In MINI120, she is assigned an unattended broadcast and wants escape. Kirara and Erika voluntarily enjoy doing it, solve a local cable problem and later decline to replace the absent host permanently. Their willingness does not mean Iroha should enjoy the same work, and their refusal of permanent replacement recognizes someone else's place without proving that person will return. The unexpected pleasure of helping and the lack of a promised equipment outcome matter independently of official publicity. Iroha's contact permission is not transmission of a message or permission for every future interruption. ([MINI32][PS35], §12.)

Makoto's regard for difference is not constant. MAIN's screw metaphor gives way, after local recovery, to a speech about freedom requiring continuing choice. EVENT860 depicts her rejecting an order to keep Iroha by force and refusing Satsuki's suggestion that obedience can count as freedom. These are consequential literal positions, not merely ironic decoration. Yet the same source preserves costly decisions, inadequately answered labor objections, a desire for Iroha's apology and a plan to shift new ship costs onto Prefects. The ensemble can identify a defended principle without inventing a stable decision rule honored in every setting. ([MAIN departure][PS10], [aftermath][PS20]; [summer account][PS04], 004,011,014.)

Satsuki and Chiaki also take different routes from office into peer contribution. Satsuki professes no-harm intentions and remembers resisting the Emperor, but proposed testing carries unverified assumptions about Sensei's tolerance, and the experiment is expressly not performed. Her archive history is valuable self-report with unknown staff and incomplete proof of disposal. Chiaki asks what comes after making everything Gehenna; Shoko's evasive answer motivates a hunch, not verified knowledge of a covert program. Chiaki later shares an actual threat report that changes the coalition's timing. A morally unified picture would blur ethical rhetoric, questions, investigations, reports and executed work. ([Satsuki project account][PS09], [laboratory account][PS12]; [Chiaki interview][PS11], [accelerated plan][PS17].)

Ibuki's useful-work enthusiasm is not reducible to a place in that hierarchy. She wants to help with the audit; she helps with local preparations; she wants to contribute during the drift once she recognizes the problem. Adults decide she is too young for the MAIN rebel club without giving her current view. The protective exclusion and her separate ability to know, choose and help should coexist in the reading. The difference between child participation and assignment to adult danger is a recurring boundary, not an invitation to measure her worth by institutional output. ([GROUP account][PS05]; [party account][PS02],002; [summer account][PS04],005; [coalition][PS13], u0046–0065.)

This study accordingly leaves the separate institutional home to decide the governance question in full: actual authority, budget changes, office procedures, resource harm and restitution. Here those matters enter where they alter company, gratitude, burden and the ability to refuse. A generous photo placement for Ibuki can be a genuine local adjustment while a punitive audit remains unjustified. Shared affection does not make all actions within the office share one moral or evidentiary state. ([Festival trip][PS03],003; [GROUP account][PS05], audit and ending.)

## 5. Ordinary life: pleasure, appetite, play and memory as ends

The ordinary repertoire is not filler between the “real” public events. Ibuki's pudding is first a wanted dessert, not a symbol invented for Makoto's education. The search and office visit also produce actual play, admiration of kind people, a changed game rule and a wish to meet again. Aru's wanted black coffee and its bitter result close the encounter on a different appetite; Kayoko's milk suggestion is not an enacted drink. These details refuse to make every participant's experience point toward the same lesson. They preserve a social occasion with pleasures, disappointments and future invitations that need not become durable contracts to be meaningful. ([MINI32][PS35], §14, MINI15030.)

The group audit's cocoa similarly belongs first to Ibuki's own want. Its later use as a criterion does not retroactively make her request manipulative. She seeks a useful role and refreshments; Iroha turns what is missing into a bargaining opportunity under Makoto's punitive brief. The distinction matters because a child can be implicated in a use of her wishes without having designed it. It also prevents rescuing Iroha from criticism by claiming any action in Ibuki's name is what the child chose. A recipient's want and another member's political employment of it have different authors. ([GROUP account][PS05],1902 audit sequence.)

EVENT860 begins with a trip's desired equipment and supplies: snacks, a toothbrush, pajamas and company. That anticipation remains part of the actual event even after the disaster. Ibuki enjoys an improvised meal and dolphin company, helps with a frightened member's hand and plays with ship roles. The written account does not provide a food-safety audit, but a lack of that audit is no reason to deny represented enjoyment. Likewise a personal photograph is possible when members actually assent to posing; an earlier ignored refusal cannot be folded into that later assent. Ordinary pleasure has precise recipients, modes and moments. ([Summer account][PS04],001–003,005,012–013.)

These ordinary ends also carry negative evidence. A failed outing remains a failure even if another game succeeds. A wish to work remains a wish when no job is enacted. A meal invitation is not food consumed; received gratitude is not consent to indefinite service. The study retains small satisfactions as satisfactions and incomplete wants as incomplete. Their value does not depend on the later public use to which an interpreter can put them. This is why pleasure and refusal can challenge the benevolent-family and manipulative-office readings at the same time. ([Private account][PS01],502–510,546; [MINI32][PS35],§§12,14.)

## 6. Named duty P3-REL-MAKOTO-IBUKI: selective affection meets a wider promise

### 6.1 The direction and its unequal stakes

Makoto→Ibuki is a direction of attention whose giver often wants an answer back: admiration, reassurance, a place beside the child, or restored favor. Ibuki→Makoto includes wanted play, worry for her loneliness, forgiveness and requests for other people's benefit. The two are not identical motivations exchanged symmetrically. Makoto holds office and can mobilize resources; Ibuki's choices are local and situated in adult company. The meaningful reciprocity is therefore not equal power but a visible capacity to answer, refuse and alter the terms of closeness. Reading only Makoto's declared affection would miss the very feedback through which this relationship becomes intelligible. ([MINI32][PS35],§§2,14; [MAIN return visit][PS14]; [Final rescue][PS33].)

The first MINI pudding episode already differentiates regret. Makoto boasts about theft and lacks remorse while discussing an abstract victim; when she recognizes Ibuki's pudding, she acknowledges fault and apologizes. The source gives no shown replacement or accepted apology at that point. That pivot is real selective responsiveness, with a serious contrary implication: another person's equal grievance did not initially command the same concern. Ibuki's question about whether wanting her pudding was bad makes the recipient's uncertainty visible, rather than simply ratifying the leader's affection. The scene warrants neither “Makoto cannot apologize” nor “Makoto respects everyone's property because she loves Ibuki.” ([MINI32][PS35],§2, MINI70000020:u0064–0074 and surrounding account.)

The later trilogy has more demanding consequences. It begins with a repeated offense and a prior promise, so Ibuki's departure cannot be explained as a random tantrum or failure to understand kindness. Makoto's initial appeal to absent name labels evades the wider problem; Iroha insists no one's pudding should be taken. Ibuki is lost and guilty about harsh words, but these feelings do not retract her objection to the theft. Aru's escort offer is refused. The audience must preserve a child who is both vulnerable and capable of withholding the return that adults want. Concern for her whereabouts is not an entitlement to make her answer disappear. ([MINI32][PS35], MINI15010:u0002–0097.)

### 6.2 Departure, chosen company and conditional return

Discovery does not complete reconciliation. Ibuki says she left of her own accord and rejects the kidnapping story. She can say she is no longer angry and still want to stay with PS68 because play with the older girls is pleasant. This distinguishes forgiving a feeling from accepting a proposed itinerary. Haruka's wish for her company and Aru's office invitation create an actual alternative social occasion, not permanent adoption or a right to keep her. Makoto's care is tested precisely because Ibuki can find wanted company elsewhere. If her value were only to mirror the chair's benevolence, this interval would be narratively unnecessary. ([MINI32][PS35], MINI15020:u0025–0077.)

At the office, Ibuki interprets Aru's rhetoric through observed kindness rather than accepting a self-description automatically. She wins a balance game and wants a different rule. These are small acts of judgment and initiative before Makoto arrives. They matter to the named duty because the later request is authored by a recipient already doing more than waiting to be rescued. Her independence does not have to become adult political knowledge to be substantial. The office is a place of pleasure and negotiated company, while its registration, address disclosure and legal status remain separately reported or contested. ([MINI32][PS35], MINI15030, play and office-boundary account.)

The apology then produces the strongest local revision. Ibuki's condition is that Makoto take nobody's pudding. Makoto's finger promise and Ibuki's forgiveness are represented, so “nothing changes” is too weak a reading. But the change is to the terms of this encounter, not a verified permanent policy. Makoto's ten replacement puddings are reported, and actual handing-over, eating or later universal compliance is not supplied. The relation therefore achieves a widened acknowledgment and consent to renewed company, without acquiring evidence about every future action. The wider promise is both a criticism of selective care and an actual end within it. ([MINI32][PS35], MINI15030:u0088–0114.)

### 6.3 Care beyond the apology and its adverse cases

Other contexts show attention that cannot be reduced to an attempt to buy forgiveness. On the festival trip, Makoto is willing to stand at the photograph's edge if Ibuki looks good at the center. During the summer drift, she immediately denies Ibuki's self-blame for the bad rental decision and takes the first entry into a dangerous ship rather than delegating it to the child. She draws pursuit away in the pirate encounter. A bad organizer can still make actual protective acts, and these acts have specific costs and recipients. Their acknowledgment is not an instruction to excuse her earlier choices or ignore Iroha's burden. ([Festival trip][PS03],003; [summer account][PS04],002,005,007.)

The same summer sequence refuses an ideal-parent conclusion. Makoto plans around her own triumph, wants an apology from Iroha after that imagined success, and contributes to the unrecognized labor that makes Iroha refuse work. After recovery, Ibuki urges reconciliation, while Iroha asks her to wait; the narrative does not supply the mutual apology a benevolent-family reading might expect. Ibuki and Chiaki say the quarrel shows love, but Iroha rejects that simple conclusion. A child's affectionate reading is a meaningful perspective, not an authorial certification that anger is secretly affection or that an unwilling member has assented. ([Summer account][PS04],004,010–011.)

Eden makes selective care's ethical limits harder to evade. Makoto imagines a formal Schale visit as an anti-Prefect alliance until Iroha corrects her. Later she self-claims prior collusion with Arius, a sham acceptance of Eden and intentions to remove others; Ibuki notices boxes before a second explosion. The exact devices, agreement, fates and complete causal chain are not all inspected, but Makoto's admitted destructive intent and the child's exposed position are serious contrary evidence. A favorite's presence does not demonstrate good judgment on that favorite's behalf. Subsequent reported rescue and epilogue rest show survival and care without converting the gamble into harmless theater. ([Eden formal visit][PS24]; [collusion][PS26],u0039–0059; [rescue report][PS29]; [epilogue][PS30].)

Final puts the same selective affection in a different public result. Toramaru arrives, Iroha deploys it and a local danger is mostly cleared. Makoto says she timed the help because Ibuki loves the ninjas and she wants favor after a pudding dispute; Ibuki says she is no longer upset and asked them to help. These are distinct motive accounts beside actual intervention and reported no injuries. There is no need to invent either wholly selfish fraud or wholly selfless redemption. A child can redirect a leader toward a real good whose beneficiaries exceed the favored relationship. The scene cannot prove the information network, that Makoto arranged the threat, or that it is the same offense as either MINI context. ([Final rescue][PS33],scene001:u0022–0061;scene002:u0001–0024.)

### 6.4 MAIN's loneliness, freedom and ominous remainder

MAIN provides a different encounter with Ibuki's choice. After Iroha leaves, Makoto's busy isolation and Ibuki's loneliness become visible. Ibuki stays when Iroha offers an alternative because she worries Makoto will be lonely. This is neither endorsement of the changed regime nor proof of a safe environment. It is a child's reason for company. Later Ibuki's questions pull Makoto's attention from competence toward missing Iroha and recall admired rebellion; Makoto denies the child's blame and tells her she may do what she wants. That local encouragement is important precisely because the surrounding public conduct has made free choice dangerous. ([MAIN departure][PS10]; [Chiaki interview][PS11]; [return visit][PS14],u0001–0110.)

The memory/log interruption must remain an unresolved narrative seam. Its association with Makoto's headache and Ibuki's reminder does not identify a witnessed archive, a physical device or an operator, and the later legacy speculation is explicitly conditional. In C2E021, the suggestion that Ibuki could be a “true legacy” is Makoto's interpretation, not a confirmed role, capability, motive or threat from the child. To give that ominous line priority over her ordinary desires would repeat the instrumental logic the synthesis is examining. The plot can worry about how adults interpret her without replacing her authored wants with a hidden-system identity. ([MAIN return visit][PS14],u0089–0110; [legacy ending][PS21],u0096–0102.)

Makoto's named direction consequently remains ambivalent with real local changes. She can apologize, spare blame, take risks, relocate herself in a photograph, accept a wider promise and encourage choice. She can also seek admiration, repeat an offense, expose Ibuki to a disastrous bargain and interpret her through an unknown legacy. Ibuki's affection does not erase those adverse cases; her refusal does not erase affection. The relation's substantial argument is the recipient's capacity to make closeness conditional and direct selective care outward, while a powerful giver remains responsible for people beyond that recipient. ([MINI32][PS35]; [summer account][PS04]; [Eden collusion][PS26]; [Final rescue][PS33]; [MAIN legacy ending][PS21].)

## 7. Named duty P3-REL-IROHA-IBUKI: practical protection, wanted rest and the child's answer

### 7.1 A caretaker who has a life beyond care

Iroha→Ibuki is often practical: arranging company, leading by the hand, preparing or carrying burdens, explaining, checking a wish and accepting an answer. Ibuki→Iroha includes wanted presence, enjoyment of offered care, worry about anger and an ability to refuse the itinerary that care proposes. The direction is distinct from Makoto's desire for favor. It cannot be summarized as the only responsible adult substitute because Iroha is herself a student with wanted rest, embarrassment, grievances and imperfect judgments. Her private reading, sofa, coffee and dinner establish ends outside constant service, not evidence that she secretly wishes to abandon every relationship. ([Private account][PS01],504; [festival trip][PS03],003; [MAIN return visit][PS14]; [summer account][PS04].)

MINI makes that independence visible. Iroha does cleanup and paperwork, plays with Ibuki and welcomes volunteers who enjoy the broadcast assignment she wants to escape. The volunteers' pleasure is not a rebuke to her preference. Keeping Ibuki at home during the Red Winter visit is a protective judgment, but it supplies no observed prior injury or omniscient forecast. Care involves acting under uncertainty, and the source allows that judgment to remain attributed. There is no reason to convert competence into perfect knowledge or willingness into an obligation to accept all future work. ([MINI32][PS35],§§2–3,12.)

### 7.2 The audit's cocoa and disputed tears

GROUP1902 supplies the strongest negative test of Iroha's claim to speak for Ibuki. Makoto sends her to find any fault, not conduct an open inquiry. Iroha reluctantly describes it as only an audit, then uses uncommunicated newspaper-display rules and missing cocoa to secure revisions. Ibuki's eager useful work and cocoa request do not mean she authored this punitive design. Iroha admits the chair's brief to find fault and asks that it be forgotten. The distinction between Ibuki's legitimate wish and Iroha's institutional employment of it prevents a sentimental account from making the child responsible for a penalty she did not choose. ([GROUP account][PS05],1902 audit sequence.)

The fall and tears make the same distinction explicit. Ibuki says she is fine and will not cry. Iroha treats the incident as making her cry, pushes the budget to zero and invokes Makoto's likely anger while calling the result lenient. These are opposing literal positions, not mutually reinforcing observations of the child's clinical state. Iroha may be protective, strategic, angry or combining motives; the account does not have to select an unprinted private intention to show that her rationale overrides Ibuki's answer. The relation's negative case is thus concrete: speaking **for** a cared-for person can suppress what that person actually says. ([GROUP account][PS05],1902 fall/revision sequence.)

The ending limits but does not erase the wrong. Earlier revisions actually occur in the represented sequence. The final zero-budget and training allocation still require formal processing, so it is false to declare a completed permanent deprivation on that basis. The subsequent gunfire, explosion and collapse are hedged aftermath, with no independently identified shooter, confrontation or restitution. Iroha's audit cannot be acquitted by an unspecified comic comeuppance, and no full office outcome is needed to recognize the local use of Ibuki's hurt as leverage. The institutional home owns the wider judgment; this named duty owns the displacement of the recipient's voice. ([GROUP account][PS05],audit ending and source-actor cautions.)

### 7.3 Protection can enable refusal

The MINI pudding sequence offers a contrasting response to the child's answer. Iroha rejects Makoto's claim that an unlabeled pudding is available: no one's pudding should be taken. When Ibuki is found, her refusal to return and wish to keep playing remain part of the encounter. The search does not end with an automatic transfer back to the office. By the final reunion, Iroha and Satsuki thank PS68, while the desk offer and Aru's refusal remain a separate optional exchange. This care is compatible with other people's company rather than a claim of exclusive possession. ([MINI32][PS35],MINI15010–15030.)

MAIN's visit makes the enabling alternative even clearer. Iroha checks on the lonely Ibuki while remaining outside the changed organization. The armband she still carries is not an explained formal attachment. She can comb hair, read and bring Ibuki away; Ibuki wants these things but chooses to stay with Makoto. Iroha asks whether she really wishes to do so and accepts it, promising to return. Neither the promise nor the offer is an accomplished move, a custody agreement or a comprehensive safety assessment. The represented achievement is that the child is offered company and can decline it without losing care. ([MAIN return visit][PS14],u0001–0063.)

Ibuki's reason also constrains Iroha's protective interpretation. She worries about Makoto's loneliness, which Iroha cannot resolve simply by taking her away. The child is not wrong by definition because her reason is relational rather than strategic. Nor is she right about all risks because the source lets her choose. This is a bounded recipient judgment that deserves preservation. Iroha's acceptance is stronger evidence of respect than an interpreter's imagined better outcome, and it remains a different act from later coordinating resistance or returning to organizational work. ([MAIN return visit][PS14]; [coalition plan][PS16], [execution plan][PS18].)

### 7.4 Secrecy, anger and offered participation during the drift

EVENT860 tests Iroha's protection through unequal knowledge. She removes dessert from the rationing plan and spares Ibuki worry while managing supplies. She hopes Makoto's misleading confidence will calm the child; later Ibuki admits she knows about the drift and quarrel and wants to help as a member. The disclosure makes protective concealment partial, not proof of a malicious deception or a fully successful shelter. Ibuki has noticed enough to ask for participation. Iroha allows her to stay close, providing a limit rather than assigning her the adult danger outright. ([Summer account][PS04],003–005.)

Iroha's anger must not be swallowed by Ibuki's wish for company. She refuses work after trivialized labor and poor supplies. Makoto's apology about noise does not meet the substance of that complaint, and Satsuki's forced formal apology is insufficient. Ibuki wants her presence; the eventual company does not prove the anger vanished or that the child consented to all the adult behavior. Makoto's refusal to order Iroha to stay is a real constraint on coercion even in this mixed scene. Rest, recognition and affection remain different goods; one cannot reliably replace another. ([Summer account][PS04],004.)

The following work includes specific competent contributions without universalizing them. Iroha shoulders the heavy cannon while Ibuki contributes knowledge with a precision limit; the shot occurs, but success does not validate willpower as its physical cause. Iroha saves Makoto from the fall and later qualifies the children's “love” reading of their quarrel. She apologizes to the frightened Ibuki for raising her voice, and later apologizes to Chiaki while refusing a repeat for a photograph. These are independent acts of care, rescue, interpretation and boundary-setting, with different recipients. A single maternal label would make those differences disappear. ([Summer account][PS04],007–013.)

### 7.5 Reciprocity with a remaining independent recipient

Ibuki can respond to Iroha without becoming the person who repairs her work environment. She wants her company and pushes reconciliation, can share play and useful ideas, and experiences care that gives her options. She does not certify the audit, validate every concealed explanation or authorize unlimited photography. Iroha can welcome the child while retaining rest and while criticizing Makoto. The summer narrative's wanted group company and MAIN's acceptance of a refused exit both show reciprocal closeness that permits disagreement. The important unit is not “Iroha is good to Ibuki” but the differentiated exchange: what she offers, what she wants, what Ibuki knows, what Ibuki answers and which action follows. ([GROUP account][PS05]; [MAIN return visit][PS14]; [summer account][PS04].)

This named duty thus has an adverse case as strong as its affirmative ones. Iroha can overrule Ibuki's account in a punitive setting and honor it in a private offer. That variation does not require inventing a change between globally dated episodes. It requires retaining the action's context and its other recipients. A protector with wanted rest and actual anger is more intelligible than an always-correct parent, while a child able to refuse is more substantial than an object of optimized care. The relation remains unfinished wherever choice has been respected locally but future safety, return visits, labor distribution or durable recognition have not been shown. ([GROUP account][PS05]; [MAIN return visit][PS14]; [private account][PS01]; [summer account][PS04].)

## 10. Language, voice and source modes: answers must keep their owners

The distinction between a speaker's story and a recipient's answer is also a formal requirement. GROUP1902's source-derived locked actor labels differ from displayed textual attribution at three consequential points: s1u0002 Makoto/Ako, s1u0057 Chinatsu/Iori and s3u0058 Makoto/Iroha. The accepted argument preserves those seams, with the next coherent Iroha turn on formal processing separately legible. The study uses the maintained interpretation at that declared scope and does not claim a fresh raw reconstruction. It especially does not silently change Ibuki's refusal to cry into corroboration of Iroha's crying claim. Different modes and attributions can support a local encounter without a fabricated clean transcript. ([GROUP account][PS05],source audit and complete1902 argument.)

MAIN has comparable self-reference and response anomalies. Iroha-tagged lines in S2C1E001 boast as “this Makoto”; Makoto-tagged lines in Eden can admonish Makoto herself; a Hina tag in the recovery aftermath self-identifies as Makoto. Those are not stable voice samples for the printed actor. Inward Sensei speech receiving a reply is not proof of telepathy. Anonymous logs or sounds are not an identified operator. The independent argument therefore rests on coherent choices, reported acts and source-qualified reversals, while keeping uncertainty about fine-grained attribution. A corrected reading must retain the literal seam, not erase it by replacing every label from contextual plausibility. ([Public resource conflict][PS07]; [Eden visit][PS24], [collusion][PS26]; [MAIN aftermath][PS20]; [return visit][PS14].)

Ibuki's register can be playful, uncertain, excited or worried without being merely a cue for adults to speak through her. The party's adult-plan speech under Ibuki tags is quarantined rather than used to make the child author humiliation, capture or institutional dissolution. Final's heavily drifting second scene likewise supports local rescue and motive accounts more securely than a precise idiolect or each person's exact thanks. The important interpretive protection is to preserve securely authored child wants and refusals while refusing adult claims whose only support is a suspect tag. That preserves sparse positive evidence instead of solving the seam by discarding Ibuki. ([Party account][PS02],007–008; [Final rescue][PS33],source-form cautions.)

The private repertoire retains whole-MM and written-form differences. An interactive alternative is a route or conditional answer, not simultaneous enacted behavior. A birthday, purchase, invitation or future escape expression can disclose a want while leaving the activity unperformed. The maintained private account preserves Japanese/Korean distinctions, actorless/narrative layers and the adopted swimsuit-reading correction. This study has received that account's connected meaning; it has not freshly replayed all full original MM or inspected media. Neither high affect nor the language of proximity permits converting a particular offer into blanket consent, a canonical romance timeline or all-variant cohabitation. ([Private account][PS01],current adoption and whole-MM/mode paragraphs504,546–550.)

Photography, singing and piano also need source labels. The study can discuss an organized and taken picture, a wished-for picture, posing, torn records or promised circulation where the text supplies them. It cannot see expressions, camera angles or clothing changes from these written analytical accounts. The party's video IDs and MINI's written singing are navigation or textual events, not heard tone, performance timing or an acted intimacy. Familiarity in the words is already significant; the missing performed warrant should neither be forged nor used to discard that significance. ([MINI32][PS35],§§12,14; [party account][PS02],009–010; [summer account][PS04],012–013.)

Several repeated terms also change owners and force. Makoto's machine metaphor rejects dissent, while Chiaki treats the differences that obstruct perfect alignment as a source of interest. Makoto's later correction toward a shared Gehenna matters as a chosen formulation, not a universal technical account of how autonomy returned. A promise about nobody's pudding has a wider recipient set than an apology for Ibuki's pudding. Iroha's claim of leniency in the audit can conflict with Ibuki's actual statement. These are not interchangeable expressions of “care”; each names a speaker's proposed relation to other people's choices. ([MAIN departure][PS10]; [Chiaki interview][PS11]; [aftermath][PS20]; [MINI32][PS35],§14; [GROUP account][PS05].)

## 11. Serious competing readings

### 11.1 A benevolent family whose quarrels prove intimacy

This reading has substantial positive evidence. Members play, take hands, prepare company, apologize, accept an edge position in a photograph and rescue each other. Makoto rejects Ibuki's self-blame. Iroha offers an exit and accepts the child's refusal. The pudding promise yields actual forgiveness. Treating all that as cynical camouflage would abandon represented good ends. The reading also explains why a disagreement within wanted company can carry more hurt than a dispute with a stranger: the expectation of attention already exists.
